page.summary: Take injured-teammate triage as a real role: find the next reachable reset, heal while it is safe, and hand the job off when pressure or objective tempo changes.

verdict.recommendation: Choose this role when the team can spend time restoring health without turning the healer into a second down or abandoning a critical objective.
verdict.soloQ: Use teammate information to choose a reachable heal, then verify the reset is still safe instead of crossing the map automatically.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call the injured target, healer assignment and handoff so two players do not leave objectives for the same reset.
verdict.mainWeakness: Healing can be strategically wrong under heavy slowdown or pressure; speed stacking has diminishing returns and the role commits substantial team time.

plans.label: Healer tools
plans.why: This module supports the healer role without pretending to be a fixed four-perk build.

choices.whyItsHere: Locate injured or dying teammates before crossing the map for a heal.
Make a reachable teammate heal efficient and give injured teammates a way to find you.
Improve healing speed without requiring a particular teammate to carry the interaction.
Convert a rescue into a timely teammate heal when the reset is safe.

item.name: Med-Kit
item.why: Use a med-kit when it makes a safe reset or charge-efficient heal possible; the role does not depend on a particular add-on.

gameplay.assignment: Take the next reachable injured health state as a deliberate team job, while abandoning the heal when pressure or objective tempo makes it wrong.

priorities.situation: A teammate is injured or dying and the path is reachable.
priorities.action: Use the information tool to choose the nearest safe reset, then approach with an exit rather than crossing the map automatically.
priorities.why: Triage value comes from selecting a heal that returns a teammate to a useful job.

priorities.situation: You and the teammate can heal without pulling pressure onto the reset.
priorities.action: Start the heal with the selected speed tool or optional med-kit, and stop if the Killer turns the reset into a chase.
priorities.why: Healing speed cannot repay a down or an abandoned critical objective.

priorities.situation: You have just unhooked a teammate and the reset window is safe.
priorities.action: Use the post-unhook heal window if the teammate can finish the reset; otherwise hand the heal to a safer partner and return to the next job.
priorities.why: The rescue-triggered tool is valuable only when the unhook actually creates a safe heal.

handoffWhen: Hand off a heal when the teammate is safer with another rescuer, the Killer has changed pressure or a critical generator/rescue is uncovered.
Call who owns the reset so two teammates do not abandon the same objective.
abortWhen: Abort the heal when the Killer can reach both Survivors before the reset completes.
Stop travelling for an injured teammate when the distance or current hook state makes the reset less valuable than the uncovered team job.

soloQ: A visible injured teammate is an invitation to triage, not a command to travel; keep the nearest rescue or generator in view.
coordinatedSwf: Name the healer and reset target, then release the role when another player is safer or the team needs the healer elsewhere.

strengths: Restore team health efficiently when a safe reset is available.
weaknesses: Healing can be the wrong macro decision against heavy pressure, and losing the med-kit or its charges reduces the role's ceiling.
killerCounterplay: The Killer can change targets or pressure the reset route so the time spent seeking a heal no longer repays the team.
commonMistakes: Crossing the map for an injured teammate while a nearer rescue or critical generator is uncovered.
Treating the optional med-kit as infinite or assuming healing speed makes every reset correct.
Keeping the healer assignment after the Killer has made the reset unsafe instead of handing it off.
